node_fields.name: concept name
node_fields.topic: owning topic id; null for topic nodes
node_fields.default_order: default teaching order within the topic
node_fields.visual: interactive | simulation | algorithm | function | chart | diagram | none (optional; absent = none)

nodes.name: REST APIs and Authentication and Sessions
HTTP Protocol
nodes.description: The stateless application-layer protocol underlying the web, where clients issue requests with methods and headers and servers reply with status codes and bodies.
nodes.visual_hint: Sequence diagram of an HTTP request-response exchange.

nodes.name: URLs and DNS
nodes.description: How web resources are named by URLs and located by resolving the hostname through DNS into an IP address before connecting.

nodes.name: Client-Server Model
nodes.description: The web's architecture where browser clients request resources and servers respond, dividing responsibilities between front-end presentation and back-end logic.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram the browser-client and server request flow.

nodes.name: HTML
nodes.description: HyperText Markup Language structuring web page content as a tree of nested elements with semantic tags that browsers parse and render.

nodes.name: CSS
nodes.description: Cascading Style Sheets describing the presentation of HTML, controlling layout, colour, and typography through selectors, the box model, and cascading rules.

nodes.name: JavaScript
nodes.description: The browser's scripting language adding interactivity to pages, manipulating content and responding to events with an event-driven, single-threaded model.

nodes.name: DOM Manipulation
nodes.description: The Document Object Model representing a page as a live tree of objects that scripts traverse and mutate to update content dynamically.
nodes.visual_hint: Tree diagram of the DOM nodes of a web page.

nodes.name: React Components
nodes.description: A component-based JavaScript library building user interfaces from reusable components that render declaratively from data, reconciled through a virtual DOM.
nodes.visual_hint: Component-tree diagram of nested React components.

nodes.name: State and Props
nodes.description: React's data-flow model where props pass data down to child components and state holds local mutable data that triggers re-rendering when changed.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram props flowing down and state updates re-rendering a component tree.

nodes.name: Node.js
nodes.description: A server-side JavaScript runtime built on the V8 engine, using an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model to build scalable network applications.

nodes.name: Express and Routing
nodes.description: A minimal Node.js web framework providing routing and middleware to handle HTTP requests, compose request processing, and build server-side APIs.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram an Express request passing through routing and middleware.

nodes.name: REST APIs
nodes.description: An architectural style for web APIs modelling functionality as resources addressed by URLs and manipulated through standard HTTP methods and status codes.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram REST resources and their HTTP-method operations.

nodes.name: Authentication and Sessions
nodes.description: Mechanisms verifying user identity and maintaining logged-in state across stateless HTTP using sessions, cookies, and tokens such as JWTs.
nodes.visual_hint: Sequence diagram of authentication establishing a session.

nodes.name: Relational Databases
nodes.description: Databases organising data into tables of rows and columns, with primary and foreign keys expressing relationships, queried using SQL.

nodes.name: SQL
nodes.description: Structured Query Language for defining and manipulating relational data, expressing selection, filtering, joining, and aggregation declaratively.

nodes.name: NoSQL and MongoDB
nodes.description: Non-relational document stores like MongoDB holding schema-flexible JSON-like documents, trading relational guarantees for scalability and flexibility.

nodes.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
nodes.description: Cross-site scripting, a vulnerability where attacker-supplied scripts execute in victims' browsers, mitigated by escaping output and content security policies.

nodes.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
nodes.description: Cross-site request forgery, an attack tricking an authenticated browser into sending unintended requests, defended with anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies.

nodes.name: SQL Injection
nodes.description: An attack inserting malicious SQL through unsanitised input to manipulate database queries, prevented with parameterised queries and input validation.
